arxiv-2105-04675.title: Closed geodesics and Frøyshov invariants of hyperbolic three-manifolds
arxiv-2105-04675.creator: Francesco Lin, Michael Lipnowski
arxiv-2105-04675.description: Abstract . Frøyshov invariants are numerical invariants of rational homology three-spheres derived from gradings in monopole Floer homology. In the past few years, they have been employed to solve a wide range of problems in three and four-dimensional topology. In this paper, we look at connections with hyperbolic geometry for the class of minimal L L -spaces.

arxiv-2207-09145.title: GAFX: A General Audio Feature eXtractor
arxiv-2207-09145.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . Most machine learning models for audio tasks are dealing with a handcrafted feature, the spectrogram. However, it is still unknown whether the spectrogram could be replaced with deep learning based features. In this paper, we answer this question by comparing the different learnable neural networks extracting features with a successful spectrogram model and proposed a General Audio Feature eXtractor (GAFX) based on a dual U-Net (GAFX-U), ResNet (GAFX-R), and Attention (GAFX-A) modules.

arxiv-2303-05364.title: Hodge theory and Lagrangian fibrations on holomorphic symplectic manifolds
arxiv-2303-05364.creator: Christian Schnell
arxiv-2303-05364.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Christian Schnell. The purpose of this paper is to establish several new results about the Hodge theory of
Lagrangian fibrations on (not necessarily compact) holomorphic symplectic manifolds. In particular, we prove two beautiful recent conjectures by Maulik, Shen and Yin;
and we show, without using hyperkähler metrics, that every Lagrangian
fibration gives rise to an action by the Lie algebra

\operatorname{\mathfrak{sl}}_{3}(\mathbb{C})
(in the noncompact case) or
\operatorname{\mathfrak{sl}}_{4}(\mathbb{C})
(in the compact case).

arxiv-2312-13581.title: Understanding the Role of Large Language Models in Personalizing and Scaffolding Strategies to Combat Academic Procrastination
arxiv-2312-13581.creator: Ananya Bhattacharjee, Yuchen Zeng, Sarah Yi Xu, Dana Kulzhabayeva, Minyi Ma, Rachel Kornfield, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed, Alex Mariakakis, Mary P Czerwinski, Anastasia Kuzminykh, Michael Liut, Joseph Jay Williams
arxiv-2312-13581.description: Abstract Traditional interventions for academic procrastination often fail to capture the nuanced, individual-specific factors that underlie them. Large language models (LLMs) hold immense potential for addressing this gap by permitting open-ended inputs, including the ability to customize interventions to individuals’ unique needs. However, user expectations and potential limitations of LLMs in this context remain underexplored.

arxiv-2405-18635.title: When and How Does In-Distribution Label Help Out-of-Distribution Detection?
arxiv-2405-18635.creator: Xuefeng Du, Yiyou Sun, Yixuan Li
arxiv-2405-18635.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Xuefeng Du, Yiyou Sun, Yixuan Li. Detecting data points deviating from the training distribution is pivotal for ensuring reliable machine learning. Extensive research has been dedicated to the challenge, spanning classical anomaly detection techniques to contemporary out-of-distribution (OOD) detection approaches. While OOD detection commonly relies on supervised learning from a labeled in-distribution (ID) dataset, anomaly detection may treat the entire ID data as a single class and disregard ID labels.

arxiv-2501-14450.creator: Tatsuhiro Suga, Akira Suzuki, Yuma Tamura, Xiao Zhou
arxiv-2501-14450.description: Abstract In a reconfiguration problem, we are given two feasible solutions of a combinatorial problem and our goal is to determine whether it is possible to reconfigure one into the other, with the steps dictated by specific reconfiguration rules. Traditionally, most studies on reconfiguration problems have focused on rules that allow changing a single element at a time.

pmc-11347843.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). pmc-11728642.creator: Lydia Whitham, Mahdi Sheikh, Markus W. Hollmann, Marie-Odile Parat
pmc-11728642.description: Background/Objectives: Opium consumption was recently classified by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) monograph as carcinogenic to humans based on strong evidence for cancers of the larynx, lung, and urinary bladder, and limited evidence for cancers of the oesophagus, stomach, pancreas, and pharynx. This poses the question of a potential pro-cancer effect of pharmaceutical opioid analgesics.

pmc-12534457.title: CH7450924, a KEAP1-NRF2 interaction inhibitor, ameliorates LPS-induced multiple organ dysfunction via inflammatory pathway inhibition
pmc-12534457.creator: Masaki Hoshino, Yukari Yasui, Shun Mitsumata, Yuko Ito, Hiroki Kawauchi, Ryuichi Komatsu, Atsushi Kimbara, Naoshi Horiba
pmc-12534457.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) claims a life every few seconds worldwide and is a severe condition that can affect people of all ages. Despite the availability of various treatments, the unmet medical needs remain high. Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) is a key molecule involved in biological protection and is expected to be beneficial for MODS, but its role in ameliorating MODS remains unknown.

pmc-12655772.description: Background:Spiritual care is a critical component of holistic healthcare, significantly contributing to patients’ well-being and recovery. This study aimed to examine the relationship between spiritual competence, religiosity, and professional competence in delivering spiritual care among Iranian nursing students.
